report.summary: Reviewed harness.py chunk 1 of 4: documented claims about recall, focus-withheld, correctness, error rows, aggregation, and tier gating are mostly kept; some claims are uncheckable because they reference functions defined later in the file.
risks: eval_task_tier1 | medium | The try block catches only (ValueError, OSError); task['repo'] and other dict accesses are unguarded and could raise KeyError, contradicting the docstring's NEVER RAISES claim. | Inspect eval_task_tier1's full exception handling in later chunks; if task['repo'] is guaranteed by callers, the claim may still be broken for arbitrary task dicts.

eval_task_tier1 | medium | The focus-withheld detection relies on the shape of res['withheld'] (list of dicts with 'role' key). If semantic_slice emits a different shape, _is_focus_withheld will silently return False. | Confirm semantic_slice's output shape in slice.py; the claim about the exact shape is uncheckable from this chunk.

_group_rows_by_provenance | low | Rows missing 'label_provenance' or 'label_tier' will raise KeyError; the function's docstring does not mention this requirement. | Check callers in later chunks to see if they always include these keys.

claims.text: Tier 1 (deterministic, no LLM, the rigorous core): For each task, take the distilled semantic_slice and measure recall and compression.
claims.why: eval_task_tier1 calls semantic_slice and computes recall and compression exactly as described.

claims.text: Aggregated PER LABEL-PROVENANCE TIER ... never blended into one number
claims.why: _by_provenance is the only aggregation path and groups by provenance and tier; no top-level blended mean exists in this chunk.

claims.text: tier == 'quarantine' tasks are excluded from every headline and reported separately (see run_tier1).
claims.why: run_tier1's body is not in this chunk; the claim about quarantine exclusion cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Any task with recall < 1.0 is a slice-recall miss; we surface exactly which symbols were dropped
claims.why: eval_task_tier1 returns a 'missed' list of the must_include items not found; _tier1_aggregate counts misses and lists missed_ids.

claims.text: Arms A/B/C ... scored on BOTH recall (via _recall) and true token cost.
claims.why: The arms functions are not in this chunk; only _recall is present and used in Tier 1.

claims.text: Tier 2 ... Gated: if no provider is reachable it is skipped cleanly with a message -- Tier 2 NEVER crashes Tier 1 and NEVER makes a network call unless explicitly enabled.
claims.why: Tier 2 functions are not in this chunk.

claims.text: Gate (advisory, local-only): run_gate replays the corpus against a stored baseline.json and flags PRIMARY-tier tasks whose recall decreased
claims.why: run_gate is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Isolated: imports only structcore's stable public API.
claims.why: Imports from daedalus.structcore are index, languages.spec_for, parse.extract_units, slice.semantic_slice, and tokens (with fallback). These appear to be public API modules.

claims.text: The hardcoded TASKS plus every task persisted in the mint store ... no store file -> load_minted_tasks returns [] -> this is exactly TASKS, same order, same content.
claims.why: Implementation is `return TASKS + load_minted_tasks()`; if load_minted_tasks returns [], the result is exactly TASKS.

claims.text: Fail-closed: only the EXACT string 'primary' counts. A missing, typo'd, or otherwise unrecognized tier is treated as quarantine
claims.why: Implementation is `return label_tier == 'primary'`; any other value yields False, which callers treat as quarantine.

claims.text: Both tier buckets always exist (possibly empty) so a report renders a stable shape
claims.why: The function initializes each provenance with both 'primary' and 'quarantine' lists before appending rows.

claims.text: This is the ONLY aggregation path Tier 1 and the arms comparison use -- there is deliberately no top-level blended mean anywhere in this module.
claims.why: Arms functions are not in this chunk; cannot verify they use _by_provenance exclusively.

claims.text: CALLERS MUST PRE-FILTER OUT ERRORED ROWS AND FOCUS-WITHHELD ROWS ... folding either in would either KeyError or (worse) silently get treated as a zero
claims.why: The function accesses r['recall'], r['compression'], etc. in aggregate_fn; error rows lack these keys, focus-withheld rows also lack them, so KeyError would occur. The docstring's warning is accurate.

claims.text: error is the marker every downstream aggregator/report checks ... ABSENT, not None -- so any aggregation path that forgets to filter on error fails loudly (KeyError)
claims.why: The returned dict has no recall/compression keys, so any aggregator accessing those keys will KeyError.

claims.text: Refused as an ERRORED row ... so it takes every existing path for a degraded measurement
claims.why: It calls _task_error_row and adds correctness_task=True, so it is indeed an error row.

claims.text: the withheld block contains a role=='focus' entry -- the exact shape slice.py emits when the unconditional secret floor fires on the target itself
claims.why: The shape of res['withheld'] is defined in slice.py, which is not in this chunk; the code checks exactly for role=='focus' entries.

claims.text: There is NO recall/compression/missed (Tier 1) or recall_A/tokens_A/... (arms) key at all -- ABSENT, not a zero
claims.why: The returned dict contains only id, project, target, focus_file, focus_withheld, label_provenance, label_tier; no recall/compression keys.

claims.text: Empty label list -> recall 1.0 vacuously.
claims.why: If must_include is empty, the function returns (1.0, []) immediately.

claims.text: NEVER RAISES: a resolution failure ... is caught and returned as an ERRORED row
claims.why: The try block catches only (ValueError, OSError). However, task['repo'] on line 150 (in this chunk) is an unguarded subscript and can raise KeyError if 'repo' is missing. Also task['id'], task['target'] in the success return path can raise KeyError. The docstring claims NEVER RAISES, but only specific exceptions are caught.

claims.text: A CORRECTNESS task is refused here before anything is sliced
claims.why: The first check is `if is_correctness_task(task): return _correctness_task_row(task)`.

claims.text: Defaulted so pre-provenance task dicts ... still group as 'hand_reachable'/'primary'
claims.why: The return dict uses task.get('label_provenance', 'hand_reachable') and task.get('tier', 'primary').

observations.what: eval_task_tier1's docstring claims NEVER RAISES but the try block only catches ValueError and OSError; unguarded dict accesses like task['repo'], task['id'], task['target'] can raise KeyError.
The focus-withheld detection depends on the exact shape of semantic_slice's 'withheld' output; if that shape changes, _is_focus_withheld will silently return False instead of reporting a problem.
_group_rows_by_provenance assumes every row has 'label_provenance' and 'label_tier' keys; missing keys would raise KeyError. The docstring does not mention this precondition.
